teaser.text: CLP Holdings Limited is a power company that makes, moves and sells electricity, while also providing energy services. Its business stretches from regulated electricity bills in Hong Kong to competitive retail plans, power stations and energy projects across several markets.

stock.title: CLP stock forecast
stock.meta_description: CLP's stock forecast gives weighted bear, base and bull scenarios and tests them against project delivery, cash flow and valuation.
stock.opening: CLP's weighted price is HK$81.48 in October 2027, with a 55% base case, a 25% bear case and a 20% bull case. CLP's outcome hinges on project delivery, Australian recovery and cash conversion.
stock.closing: The full CLP memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could CLP's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is HK$81.48. It implies a 10% total return in October 2027. At the last forecast date, it reaches HK$88.09. That implies a 27% total return in October 2029. The bear case probability is 25%. The base case is 55%. The bull case is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for CLP?

paragraphs.text: The base case rises to HK$11,500 million in 2027. It then reaches HK$12,000 million and HK$12,500 million, as Hong Kong regulated assets and demand grow while Australian competition and investment costs remain a drag. The bear case falls to HK$10,800 million, then HK$10,400 million and HK$10,000 million, reflecting weaker Australia, funding pressure and the Yallourn replacement gap. The bull case reaches HK$12,200 million, then HK$13,300 million and HK$14,500 million, requiring stronger Hong Kong demand, stable Australian retail and successful storage projects. Data-centre sales already rose 7.5% in 2025, while EnergyAustralia’s operating contribution fell from HK$591 million to HK$85 million.

blocks.heading: How much cash does CLP really make?

paragraphs.text: A conservative free-cash-flow measure starts with cash from operations and subtracts capital spending, lease payments and interest. It asks what remains after running the business, funding its assets and paying finance costs. Construction cycles are lumpy, so a negative year may reflect heavy investment rather than weak operations; a positive year may still be insufficient to replace ageing equipment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for CLP today?

paragraphs.text: Valuation multiples describe the price from different angles. P/E compares the share price with earnings, EV/revenue compares the whole business with its sales, and price-to-book compares the market value with recorded shareholders’ equity. None proves that CLP is cheap or expensive alone.

dividend.title: CLP dividend: payments and cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: CLP dividend payments rose from HK$3.10 to HK$3.20; 2025 free cash flow was below dividends paid, with projects shaping future payouts.
dividend.opening: CLP paid dividends per share that rose from HK$3.10 to HK$3.20 across the period provided. In 2025, free cash flow was HK$6,729 million while dividends paid were HK$7,958 million.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers how CLP’s business works, how its rivals compare, how management is executing, and which risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: How much does CLP pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise cautiously in the base case. The first base figure is HK$3.23. It rises to HK$3.26, then HK$3.29. The bear case freezes DPS at HK$3.20 because investment needs and weak cash coverage could prevent increases. The bull case reaches HK$3.25, then HK$3.35 and HK$3.45 if earnings convert into cash more effectively. CLP’s DPS rose from HK$3.10 to HK$3.20 across the period provided, but 2025 free cash flow of HK$6,729 million was below dividends paid of HK$7,958 million.

blocks.heading: Does CLP’s dividend come from its cash?

paragraphs.text: CLP uses cash for power assets and dividends, but current free cash flow does not cover payouts in every year. In 2025, free cash flow was HK$6,729 million while dividends paid were HK$7,958 million. The same broad pattern appeared in 2024 and 2021, while free cash flow exceeded payouts by HK$328 million in 2023. Shareholders received cash through dividends rather than share buybacks, and CLP issued no new shares in the five years shown.

paragraphs.text: From 2028 into 2029, the decisive evidence will be cash conversion. If transition spending raises debt while dividends exceed free cash flow, the multiple and dividend path should weaken. If projects generate cash as planned, CLP can fund growth with less financial pressure and justify the bull valuation.

blocks.heading: What is CLP’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Cash flow needs more care because utilities continually spend on assets. CLP’s free cash flow starts with operating cash and subtracts income tax, but it does not necessarily deduct every new project. In 2025, CLP reported HK$22.6 billion of free cash flow. It also spent HK$3.2 billion on growth capital expenditure. That is why dividend coverage must be judged across the investment cycle, not from yield alone.
